key_insight: The paper shows that the linear Poisson source for wall-pressure remains inner-scaled and approximately constant at very high Reynolds number, so the observed logarithmic growth of wall-pressure variance must come from the nonlinear source.
engineering_relevance: This clarifies which turbulence mechanism drives near-wall pressure fluctuations, improving wall-modeling and pressure-prediction strategies for high-Reynolds-number aerodynamic flows.
method: Used simultaneous velocity and velocity-gradient hot-wire measurements from a single eight-sensor probe.
Compared a zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layer with a high-Reynolds-number pipe flow.
Examined inner-scaled factors in the linear pressure source and the wall-distance dependence of gradient variance.
evidence_signal: The evidence comes from experimental data up to friction Reynolds numbers of order 10^4, showing collapse of the linear-source factors and inverse wall-distance decay of the relevant inertial-layer gradient variance.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on specific canonical wall-bounded flows and hot-wire measurements, so extrapolation to more complex geometries or strongly noncanonical conditions should be done cautiously.
paper_title: An Inner-Scaled Linear Contribution to Wall-Pressure Variance at High Reynolds Number
